# General normal-conditional ball inequalities and surface midpoint repair

This argument bypasses smooth normal foliations. Its new step is to
truncate the ACTUAL bodies by countably many balls, transfer the established
surface-area measure inequality to conditional ball masses, and then use
Radon differentiation. No rank identity for the Gauss map is assumed.

Dependencies are stated explicitly. The geometric ones already proved in
this workspace are contact surface-area domination and the measure-level
Brunn--Minkowski inequality for surface-area measures. The ordinary
conditional-face absolute-continuity theorem is the Caravenna--Daneri
background theorem; its transfer to normal disintegration is explained in
Section 2 and proved fully in
`candidate f38040720425d155`.
Only absolute continuity/equivalence is needed, not continuity
or local boundedness of a conditional density.

## 1. Geometric data and the measure-level input

Let d>=2 and let A,B,K be convex bodies in R^d with

    M=(A+B)/2 subset K,
    Z={n:h_K(n)=[h_A(n)+h_B(n)]/2}.

Let eta_i denote surface measure on the physical normal bundle (n,x),
and S_i its normal marginal, for i=A,B,K. Write

    lambda=S_A+S_B+S_K,
    eta_i(dn,dx)=lambda(dn) mu_(i,n)(dx).          (1)

These are unnormalized conditional measures relative to ONE reference
lambda. Their total masses are dS_i/dlambda. They are supported on the
corresponding exposed faces whenever their mass is nonzero.

Put r=d-1 and, for positive a,b, define

    P_r(a,b)=[(a^(1/r)+b^(1/r))/2]^r.

The established area-measure theorem implies that for any two convex
bodies L_-,L_+, the area measure of their midpoint body dominates the
measure with this power-mean density relative to a common reference.
See Section 6 of
`candidate d332d092619053f4`.

Only the part where BOTH endpoint densities are positive will be used.
That part also follows directly from the proved common-submeasure theorem:
for 0<s<1 apply it to L_-/(2(1-s)) and L_+/(2s), with weights 1-s,s.
Their weighted sum is (L_-+L_+)/2. Taking the countable supremum over
rational s balances the two scaled endpoint densities and yields P_r.
This shortcut does NOT give the residual term where one density vanishes;
the present proof never needs that residual.

We also use the proved contact fact: if L subset K and h_L=h_K on a
normal set T, then S_L restricted to T is dominated by S_K restricted
to T. Its proof is physical: regular boundary points of L with a contact
normal are the same boundary points of K, up to surface-null singular
sets. See `candidate 0c3c4405d9ae2dd3`.

## 2. Ordinary conditional-face background and normal labels

For surface-almost every point of a convex body, the outer normal is
unique and the point belongs to the relative interior of its exposed
face. The conditional-face disintegration theorem identifies the
conditional surface law there with a measure equivalent to Hausdorff
measure of that face's affine dimension. The latter includes point masses
for zero-dimensional faces.

The normal cone is constant on the relative interior of a face. Thus a
relevant relative-interior face containing a surface-regular point has
one unique normal throughout its relative interior. On the full surface
measure set just described, the face label and its normal label determine
one another. Consequently the conditional laws in (1), at normals where
they have positive mass, are equivalent to H_(m_i) on the corresponding
relative-interior exposed face, with m_i its affine dimension. Their
support is the whole closed face.

This is the only face-disintegration background used below. It is the
ordinary theorem of Caravenna and Daneri, applied in local convex graph
charts; the graph-to-surface factor is constant on a fixed normal fiber.
The full chart-to-normal transfer and the overlapping-chart propagation
needed for global reverse absolute continuity are proved in Sections
4-5 of `candidate f38040720425d155`.
Its Section 6 tracks the scalar Radon--Nikodym weights for the common
reference lambda in (1). Equivalence is asserted for the FULL surface
conditional capacities; arbitrary selected submeasures inherit domination
and absolute continuity, not necessarily reverse absolute continuity.
See [The Disintegration of the Lebesgue Measure on the Faces of a Convex
Function](https://cvgmt.sns.it/media/doc/paper/1434/disFacceConvCD.pdf).
In particular, no smooth or rectifiable normal manifold is inferred from
that result.

## 3. Exact localization by a ball cut

Let L be a convex body, let B(c,a) be an OPEN ball, and assume
L'=L intersect closed B(c,a) is a convex body. Define the open normal set

    V_(L,c,a)={v:h_L(v)<v dot c+a}.                (2)

On this normal set, the normal surface measure of L' is exactly the
original physical surface measure restricted to the open ball:

    S_(L') restricted to V
       =(normal)_*(1_(B(c,a)) eta_L) restricted to V.                (3)

Proof. At a regular boundary point x of L' with unique normal v in V,
x cannot be on the cutting sphere. Otherwise the sphere's normal
(x-c)/a belongs to the normal cone of L'. Uniqueness makes it equal to
v, so x=c+a v. Since x belongs to L this would give
v dot c+a<=h_L(v), contradicting (2). Hence x lies inside the open ball,
where L' and L have the same local boundary and the same regular normal.
Conversely every regular boundary point of L inside the open ball remains
a regular boundary point of L' with the same normal. Singular boundary
points have zero ordinary surface measure for both convex bodies. This
proves (3), without discarding a positive-measure boundary coincidence.

If L(n) intersects the OPEN ball, then n belongs to V: for a point x of
that intersection, h_L(n)-n dot c=n dot(x-c)<a. Such an intersection also
ensures L' is full dimensional, since an ambient ball about x meets the
interior of the full-dimensional body L.

## 4. One full-measure normal set for every conditional ball inequality

Choose all balls with rational centers and positive rational radii. For
each ordered pair B_-=B(c_-,a_-), B_+=B(c_+,a_+), set

    c_0=(c_-+c_+)/2,   a_0=(a_-+a_+)/2,
    B_0=B(c_0,a_0).

These are still countably many balls. Consider the truncated bodies

    A'=A intersect closed B_-,
    B'=B intersect closed B_+,
    K'=K intersect closed B_0.

Whenever the two endpoint conditional open-ball masses are positive,
the corresponding exposed faces intersect the two open balls. The
truncated endpoint bodies are then full dimensional and retain their
original support values at that normal. Their midpoint belongs to the
middle open ball, so K' is also full dimensional and retains h_K there.
Moreover

    (A'+B')/2 subset K'

by convexity of K and the elementary midpoint inclusion for balls.

At a normal n in Z with both endpoint conditional masses positive, all
three strict conditions (2) hold, and the midpoint of A',B' has tight
support against K'. Apply surface-area power-mean domination to A',B',
then contact domination to their midpoint and K'. On the relevant open
normal sets, (3) identifies their Radon--Nikodym densities relative to
lambda as the corresponding conditional open-ball masses. Thus, outside
a null set depending on this ball pair,

    mu_(K,n)(B_0)
       >=P_r(mu_(A,n)(B_-),mu_(B,n)(B_+))           (4)

whenever n belongs to Z and BOTH endpoint masses are positive.

Here are the measure details behind this localization. On the open
intersection of the three V's, each truncated area's normal measure is
absolutely continuous with respect to lambda by (3). Restricting the
power-mean measure inequality there gives its homogeneous power mean of
those lambda-densities. On the contact set the middle truncated measure
dominates that measure. The set defined by positive conditional ball
masses is Borel and lies in this contact set up to the already fixed
null sets where the conditional supports are not the actual faces.
Thus the resulting inequality is an ordinary Radon--Nikodym inequality
on a Borel set. No independent weak limits of intersected measures occur.

Take the union of all exceptional sets for the countably many rational
ball pairs, and include the exceptional sets in (1)-(3). Outside that
ONE lambda-null set, (4) holds for all rational ball pairs.

It then holds for ALL open ball pairs. Given arbitrary B(c_i,a_i),
choose rational centers c_i,j and radii a_i,j tending to them with

    |c_i,j-c_i|+a_i,j<a_i.

Their open balls lie inside the desired balls and eventually contain
every point of those open balls. Dominated convergence gives convergence
of the input conditional masses. The averaged rational balls lie inside
the desired averaged open ball. Therefore its middle mass is at least
the limit of the right sides of (4). This proves (4) for all centers and
radii on the SAME full-measure normal set, including centers chosen
after n is known.

## 5. Face dimensions and tangent spaces must align

Fix a normal n in that full-measure set with n in Z and both endpoint
conditional laws nonzero. Drop n from notation. Let m_A,m_B,m_K be
their actual exposed-face dimensions. The middle law is nonzero by (4).
All three laws have the equivalence stated in Section 2.

Fix ANY x in supp mu_A. For every epsilon>0, mu_A(B_epsilon(x))>0.
For y in supp mu_B, apply (4) with equal radii epsilon. Since
P_r(a,b)>=2^(-r)b when a,b>0,

    mu_K(B_epsilon((x+y)/2))
       >=2^(-r) mu_B(B_epsilon(y)).               (5)

Let T(y)=(x+y)/2 and nu=T_*mu_B. If m_B>0, ordinary differentiation of
the density of mu_B in its m_B-dimensional affine space gives, for
mu_B-almost every y,

    mu_B(B_epsilon(y))/nu(B_epsilon(T(y)))
      =mu_B(B_epsilon(y))/mu_B(B_(2epsilon)(y))
       ->2^(-m_B).                               (6)

The finite positive density required here holds almost everywhere by
the conditional absolute continuity/equivalence. If m_B=0 the same ratio
equals one at its single support point for all sufficiently small radii.

The differentiation theorem for finite Radon measures, applied to mu_K
relative to nu using ambient balls, now gives

    d(mu_K)_ac/dnu>=2^(-(r+m_B))    nu-almost everywhere.

In particular nu is absolutely continuous with respect to mu_K. If
m_K>m_B, the affine support of nu has zero H_(m_K) measure, hence zero
mu_K measure, contradicting nu's positive mass. Thus m_K<=m_B. Reverse
the roles of A and B to obtain m_K<=m_A.

On the other hand actual exposed-face inclusion gives

    [A(n)+B(n)]/2 subset K(n),
    m_K>=dim(L_A+L_B)>=max(m_A,m_B),

where L_i is the direction space of the corresponding face. All these
inequalities force

    m_A=m_B=m_K=:m,
    L_A=L_B=L_K.                                 (7)

The averaged endpoint affine spaces consequently equal the middle face's
affine space. This proof never evaluates the target density at a possibly
exceptional lower-dimensional midpoint set, and uses no local boundedness
claim for that density.

## 6. A pointwise envelope valid for every good endpoint pair

Assume m>=1 and use the common Euclidean tangent coordinates furnished
by (7), with compatible affine origins. Let omega_m be the volume of
the unit m-ball. On the full-measure Borel differentiation set E_i for
each endpoint conditional law, define

    f_i(x)=lim_(epsilon->0)
             mu_i(B_epsilon(x))/(omega_m epsilon^m),

so f_i is finite and positive there. At a middle point z define the
Borel upper-density representative

    g_K^+(z)=limsup_(epsilon->0)
             mu_K(B_epsilon(z))/(omega_m epsilon^m).                (8)

It agrees with the usual density of mu_K almost everywhere in its affine
space, but it may be infinite on a null set.

For EVERY pair x in E_A, y in E_B, equation (4) with equal ball radii,
its degree-one homogeneity, and (8) give

    g_K^+((x+y)/2)>=P_r(f_A(x),f_B(y))
       >=[(f_A(x)^(-1/m)+f_B(y)^(-1/m))/2]^(-m).   (9)

Thus exceptional target points are explicitly allowed. They have not
been silently removed from possible midpoint tuples. Since (4) held for
all ball centers on one common normal set, (9) is a pointwise statement
for every pair in the marginal full-measure sets E_A times E_B.

## 7. Selection with measurable, possibly unbounded density ceilings

Let gamma_A<=mu_A and gamma_B<=mu_B have equal finite mass, and let an
old coupling have midpoint law rho_old. The compact strongly convex
surplus argument still works when f_A,f_B are measurable and not bounded.
Here are the needed checks.

For a smooth globally strongly convex surplus in the m-dimensional
common face coordinates, its optimal coupling has the Lipschitz inverse
endpoint maps F_A,F_B already proved in the density-selection theorem.
The absolute continuity of gamma_A,gamma_B suffices to show that the
midpoint law rho is absolutely continuous: for an output null set N, its
Lipschitz endpoint image F_i(N) is null and
rho(N)<=gamma_i(F_i(N))=0.

The weighted area formula gives its density h the inequalities

    h(z)<=f_i(F_i(z)) |det DF_i(z)|.

These integrals are legitimate for arbitrary nonnegative measurable
weights by the weighted area formula and monotone approximation; no
essential supremum of f_i is taken. Each selected endpoint lies in E_i
rho-almost everywhere, since its marginal is gamma_i<=mu_i. The common
positive-semidefinite derivative identity and eigenvalue arithmetic-
geometric means therefore give

    h(z)<=[(f_A(F_A(z))^(-1/m)+f_B(F_B(z))^(-1/m))/2]^(-m)
         <=g_K^+(z)                  rho-almost everywhere.         (10)

The first absolute-continuity step already ensures that rho assigns zero
mass to the Lebesgue-null exceptional set where (8) differs from the
ordinary density of mu_K, including its possible infinity set. Thus

    rho<=mu_K.                                   (11)

The fixed-marginal coupling class satisfying (11) is convex and weakly
compact, since mu_K is a fixed finite measure. Every strongly convex
surplus optimizer lies in it. Smooth approximation, finite nonnegative
separation, and compact finite intersection therefore supply ONE coupling
with

    rho_old<=_cx rho,     rho<=mu_K.                (12)

All endpoint marginals remain exactly gamma_A,gamma_B. This argument
does not require the ceiling representatives to be upper semicontinuous,
bounded, or pointwise finite outside marginal full-measure sets.

If m=0, all three exposed faces are points. Their actual midpoint is the
middle point. The common endpoint mass is at most the smaller endpoint
conditional atom mass; (4) for sufficiently small balls bounds that
minimum by the middle atom mass. The old midpoint law already satisfies
(11), so no positive-dimensional density formula is used.

## 8. Assembly scope and consequences

Equations (7), (9), and (12) hold at lambda-almost every tight normal
where the two endpoint conditional measures have positive mass. Thus
they apply to every actual balanced endpoint crossflow, whose common
normal marginal is dominated by both S_A and S_B and supported on Z.

The compact feasible coupling sets in (12), expressed in the original
ambient coordinates, have the measurable marginal, domination, and
convex-test constraints handled in
`candidate 5ea88513a25f2f4b`. That selection theorem
permits choosing the couplings and their martingale lifts measurably.
The already proved source-row rebuilding then preserves the original
physical endpoint crossflows, complete source and target measures, and
all existing cap allocations while producing a midpoint law bounded by
the ACTUAL middle normal-bundle surface measure.

The density proof itself is pointwise in n and does not assert measurable
choices without that separate assembly theorem. No polytope approximation,
smooth normal stratification, or sum-to-integral replacement enters it.
Every literal closed-halfspace midpoint implication is retained by the
one selected tuple coupling. Source halfspace order and arbitrary
supporting-selector inequalities still do not follow from convex order.

For d=1 the normal fibers are the two interval endpoints with counting
surface measure; the previously proved direct endpoint argument applies.
The present theorem is a general boundary-transport repair result, not
a proof of the numerical OC depth payment.
